extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO reply periods and abandonment rules
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural standards governing computation and resetting of reply periods, availability of extensions, express/formal abandonment, petitions to reset or revive, and related timing rules during U.S. patent prosecution (MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of shortened statutory period when advisory action mailed
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant initially replies within 2 months from mailing of a final rejection and the examiner mails an advisory action before the end of 3 months from the mailing of the final rejection, the shortened statutory period will expire at the end of 3 months from the mailing of the final rejection; if the advisory action is mailed after the end of 3 months the shortened period will expire on the date the examiner mails the advisory action. In no event will the statutory period for reply expire later than 6 months from the mailing date of the final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a petition for extension is granted, the due date for a reply is computed from the date stamped or printed on the Office action with the final rejection (see MPEP § 710.01(a)). See also MPEP § 706.07(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informalities on PTOL-37 are not correctable by 1.136 extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Informalities notified on the PTOL-37 (Notice of Allowability) cannot be corrected by extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such informalities must be corrected and any required issue fee and publication fee paid within the 3-month period (i.e., the statutory period for payment of the issue fee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time to submit affidavits after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for extension of time to submit affidavits filed after final rejection are granted without prejudice to the examiner's right to question the tardiness; the examiner may deny entry of the affidavit if applicant's showing is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting the extension merely prevents abandonment while allowing the applicant to present the affidavit or take other action. Admission (or refusal) of the affidavit will not alone save the application from abandonment; prosecution to save the application must include timely, complete and proper action as required by 37 CFR 1.113. Affidavits submitted after final rejection are treated the same as amendments submitted after final rejection (see 37 CFR 1.116(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: No extensions after payment of issue fee (nonextendable 3-month period)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory (nonextendable) time period for payment of the issue fee is 3 months from the date of the Notice of Allowance (35 U.S.C. 151).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If informalities (e.g., drawing corrections, supplemental declarations) remain outstanding at allowance, applicants will be notified on PTOL-37; but the three-month issue-fee period is nonextendable and special procedures apply if payment/withdrawal from issue is needed (see 37 CFR 1.313 and MPEP §1308).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two periods running — later limited-time action does not suspend earlier statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: When two different periods for reply run against an application (one regular statutory period and a later limited period set in a subsequent Office action), the running of the first period is not suspended or affected by the later ex parte limited-time action or an appeal therefrom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception exists involving suggested claims (see Chapter 2300). The examiner should identify controlling dates when multiple reply periods exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copying patent claims and effect on reply periods
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims are copied from a patent and all such copied claims are rejected, two different reply periods can arise; the controlling date of the statutory period is the date of the last unanswered Office action on the claims other than the copied patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ex parte Milton and Chapter 2300 for related practice; copying claims from a patent (unless suggested by the Office) generally does not constitute a reply that will save the application from abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due date falling on Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday
rubrics_metrics.description: When the last day for taking any action or paying any fee at the USPTO falls on Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the action may be taken or the fee paid on the next succeeding business day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calendar days are intended when periods are specified in days. This rule also extends the 12-month pendency of provisional applications when the twelfth-month anniversary falls on weekend/holiday. The Federal holiday list per 5 U.S.C. 6103(a) governs which days qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restarting a reply period when Office action contains error affecting ability to reply
rubrics_metrics.description: If a citation is incorrect or an Office action contains another error that affects applicant's ability to reply and the error is called to the Office's attention within 1 month of mailing, the Office will restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date the error is corrected if applicant requests it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the error is called to attention within the reply period but more than 1 month after the action, the Office may set a new period for reply to substantially equal the time remaining in the original period. The new period must be at least 1 month and runs from the date the error is corrected. See MPEP §707.05(g) for record-correction procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remailing or supplementary Office actions reset reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: When an action is remailed the action should be redated because the remailing date establishes the beginning of the period for reply. A supplementary action after a rejection that explains references more fully establishes a new date from which the statutory period runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For remailing see MPEP §707.13 and for IFW processing see the IFW Manual. Case law (e.g., Ex parte Gourtoff) supports remailing date as start of period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error discovered after expiration — period not restarted without extension fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If an error in citation or other defective Office action is called to the Office's attention after the expiration of the period for reply, the period will not be restarted and any appropriate extension fee will be required to render a reply timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office letter correcting the error will note that the time period for reply remains as previously set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to reset period due to late receipt of Office action — basic criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a petition to restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date of receipt at the correspondence address when: (A) petition filed within 2 weeks of date of receipt at correspondence address; (B) a substantial portion of the set reply period had elapsed on the date of receipt (e.g., at least 1 month of a 2- or 3-month reply period had elapsed); and (C) the petition includes evidence of the date of receipt at the correspondence address and a statement explaining how the evidence establishes that date of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority to decide such petitions is delegated to the Technology Center Director where applicable. See the USPTO Notice “Petition to reset a period for response due to late receipt of a PTO action,” 1160 O.G. 14 (1994). There is no absolute statutory obligation to restart shortened periods over 30 days, but the procedures above are available when a substantial portion of the period elapsed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to reset period due to postmark date later than mail date printed on Office action — criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a petition to restart the previously set period for reply to run from the postmark date on the Office mailing envelope when: (A) petition filed within 2 weeks of date of receipt at the correspondence address; (B) the reply period was for payment of the issue fee, or the reply period set was 1 month or 30 days; and (C) petition includes evidence showing date of receipt at correspondence address, a copy of the envelope showing the postmark date, and a statement that the Office action was received in that postmarked envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.8 and 1.10 apply to filing petitions with respect to the 2‑week filing requirement. The Office will scrutinize facts that might indicate delay after internal receipt rather than postal delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to reply within statutory period (37 CFR 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant fails to reply within the time period provided under §§ 1.134 and 1.136, the application will become abandoned unless an Office action indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution to save the application from abandonment must include a complete and proper reply as the condition of the application may require. Admission or refusal of amendments after final rejection or any amendment not responsive to the last action will not in itself save the application from abandonment. See 37 CFR 1.135(b) and MPEP §711.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide attempt to advance application may permit supplying inadvertent omission (37 CFR 1.135(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant's reply is a bona fide attempt to advance the application to final action and is substantially a complete reply to the non-final Office action but some matter was inadvertently omitted, applicant may be given a new time period under § 1.134 to supply the omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision does not apply to amendments that cancel all claims or other non-bona-fide attempts (see Ex parte Lascell and Exxon/Phillips discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment requirements (37 CFR 1.138)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be expressly abandoned by filing a written declaration of abandonment identifying the application; such declaration must be signed by a party authorized under § 1.33(b) (applicant or authorized assignee) or by an authorized attorney/agent in specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express abandonment is effective when recognized by an appropriate Office official, and the letter may specify a later effective date. Special care should be taken to ensure correct identification of the application and that abandonment is in accordance with the applicant's desires. Form PTO/SB/24 may be used for filing express abandonment; PTO/SB/24A for petitions under 1.138(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment after payment of issue fee requires petition under 37 CFR 1.313(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a letter of express abandonment is submitted in an allowed application after payment of the issue fee, the express abandonment must be accompanied by a petition to withdraw from issue under 37 CFR 1.313(c) and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The express abandonment may not be recognized unless actually received by appropriate officials in time to withdraw the application from issue. Applicants are strongly encouraged to fax or hand-carry petitions to allow sufficient processing time. If 1.313 precludes giving effect to an express abandonment, the remedy is a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 showing extraordinary circumstances where justice requires suspension of 1.313.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to avoid publication under 37 CFR 1.138(c) must be timely (generally >4 weeks)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.138(c) will not stop publication of the application unless it is recognized and acted on by the Pre‑Grant Publication Division in sufficient time to avoid publication. Generally such petitions must be received more than four weeks prior to the projected date of publication to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed within four weeks of projected publication date, petition is unlikely to prevent publication. Withdrawal from issue after payment of the issue fee may also be ineffective to avoid publication under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) (see 37 CFR 1.313(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment effects in interference proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A written declaration of abandonment signed only by an attorney/agent of record, when the application is the subject of an interference under 35 U.S.C. 135, is not effective to terminate the interference and will not be considered until after ex parte prosecution is resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be effective to terminate an interference, abandonment must be signed by the inventor with written consent of the assignee where there has been an assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive an abandoned application — requirements (37 CFR 1.137)
rubrics_metrics.description: To revive an application abandoned for failure to reply, a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 must be accompanied by: (1) the required reply (already filed), (2) a showing that the entire delay was unavoidable (1.137(a)) or a statement that it was unintentional (1.137(b)), (3) any terminal disclaimer required under 1.137(d), and (4) the petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The showing for 'unavoidable' requires statements of fact establishing both the cause of the delay to the reply and any delay between abandonment and filing the petition were unavoidable. For 'unintentional' a statement suffices but Director may require more information. No consideration of the petition's substance will occur until the fee is received. Different fees and documentary requirements apply depending on whether the ground is 'unavoidable' or 'unintentional'; terminal disclaimer rules apply to certain older applications (designs, pre‑1995 utility/plant filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency of reply may cause abandonment — examiner form paragraphs and notice practice
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed within the statutory period may nonetheless be insufficiently responsive and lead to abandonment; the examiner should notify applicant using the Notice of Abandonment form PTOL‑1432 and may use prescribed form paragraphs (e.g., ¶7.90, ¶7.98.02, ¶7.91) explaining the deficiency and advising on petitions to revive or extensions under 37 CFR 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reply appears to be a bona fide attempt with inadvertent omission, different form paragraphs (e.g., 7.95) should be used. The date for computing extensions is the date the petition and fee are filed; statutory maximums apply (no reply outside six-month statutory period and no extension for more than five months beyond the date for reply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special situations that commonly cause abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Common pitfalls: (A) copying claims from a patent when not suggested by the Office does not constitute a reply to the last Office action and will not save the application from abandonment unless the last action relied solely on the patent for the rejection of all claims; (B) withdrawal of, or failure to prosecute, an appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences may cause abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must be attentive to the dates that mark beginning and end of statutory periods in varying situations; applicant replies must reach the Office within the shortened statutory period dated from the Office action or within any extended time under 37 CFR 1.136.
